title: Blessed is the One holding the kingdom.
subtitle: A surah that pleads for its reciter
then: The Prophet ﷺ said there is a surah of thirty verses that {reward}will intercede for its reciter until he is forgiven{/reward}: this one. Ibn Kathir says Allah praises Himself and tells us {idea}the dominion is in His hand{/idea}. He deals with His creation as He wills, and no one can reverse His decree.
now: Layoffs announced at work. A new rule at the border. A diagnosis from a doctor who seems to hold your future. {idea}Every hand that seems to hold power is inside His hand.{/idea} {reward}And He gave you thirty verses to carry with you.{/reward}
old: The people with power over my life decide what happens to me.
new: The whole kingdom is in Allah's hand, and every other hand is inside His.
try: Recite Surah Al-Mulk tonight before you sleep, or listen to it.

title: Life and death were made to test who does best.
subtitle: Best in deed, not most in deeds
then: Ibn Kathir notes something small but important: {idea}Allah did not say "which of you does the most deeds"{/idea}, but which is best in deed. And though He is the Almighty, {reward}He is also Most Forgiving{/reward} to whoever turns back after disobeying.
now: You are trying to do everything: every lecture, every extra prayer, every charity drive, and burning out. {reward}The test is not volume.{/reward} {idea}It is one prayer done with your heart present, one kindness done sincerely.{/idea}
old: To pass the test, I need to pile up as many good deeds as possible.
new: Allah tests who does best, so I would rather do fewer things well.
try: Choose one prayer today and do it slowly, as well as you can, instead of rushing through.

title: Look again. Can you see any crack?
subtitle: Seven heavens without a flaw
then: Ibn Kathir says the creation is {idea}flawless, with no disunion, conflict, deficiency or defect{/idea}. So Allah invites you: look at the sky and pay attention. Ibn Abbas and others said the word means cracks. Qatadah: do you see any defect, O son of Adam?
now: You spend all day spotting flaws: in the app, in your partner, in your own face, in the meal. {idea}Tonight, go outside and do the opposite.{/idea} {reward}Look up and try to find a flaw in what the Most Merciful made.{/reward}
old: Everything has something wrong with it if you look closely.
new: The more closely I look at Allah's creation, the less I find wrong.
try: Tonight, look at the sky for two full minutes without your phone.

title: Look twice more. Your sight comes back tired.
subtitle: The eye gives up before the sky does
then: Qatadah said "twice" means look again and again. Ibn Abbas said the sight returns {idea}humbled{/idea}, and {idea}exhausted{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains: however much you look, your sight comes back worn out because it cannot detect any deficiency.
now: You have stared at your problems for months, looking for a way they prove Allah forgot you. {idea}Try staring at His work instead.{/idea} {reward}The eye gets tired long before His care runs out.{/reward}
old: If I search hard enough, I will find the gap that proves it is all random.
new: My eyes will tire long before I find a flaw in what Allah made.
try: Look closely at one leaf, flower or insect today for a full minute. Then say SubhanAllah.

title: The nearest sky, decorated with lamps.
subtitle: Beauty above, and protection too
then: After showing the heavens have no flaw, Allah shows their beauty: {reward}the nearest sky adorned with lamps{/reward}, the stars. Ibn Kathir explains it is not the stars themselves that are thrown, but {idea}meteors beneath them{/idea} that drive away the devils.
now: You see a shooting star on a camping trip and make a wish like in the films. {idea}The Quran tells you something deeper.{/idea} {reward}The sky is beautiful on purpose, and it is guarded.{/reward}
old: The night sky is pretty, but it means nothing.
new: The stars are lamps Allah placed for beauty, and the sky is guarded by His order.
try: Next time you see the stars, say the name of Allah who decorated them.

title: For those who deny their Lord, a wretched end.
subtitle: After the beauty of the sky, a sober warning

row.title: their Lord
sub: the One who made and fed them

then: Right after showing a sky without a flaw, the surah turns. Ibn Kathir says those who {trap}disbelieve in their Lord{/trap} face the torment of Hell, the worst end and a terrible destiny. The Makkan listeners lived under that same sky every night.
now: You look at the same sky, eat from the same earth, breathe the same air as everyone. {idea}The verse says "their Lord", the One who raised them.{/idea} {reward}It is a warning meant to bring you closer, while there is time.{/reward}
old: Hell is for monsters, far from ordinary people like me.
new: The danger is ignoring my own Lord, and the warning is a mercy while I can still turn.
try: Thank Allah out loud for three things He gave you today, by name.

title: They hear it roar as they are cast in.
subtitle: The Quran describes it so we never reach it
then: Ibn Jarir said the word means {trap}a sound of shouting{/trap}, heard from the Fire while it boils. The Makkans heard this verse while there was still time to change. {idea}It was a warning delivered early, out of mercy.{/idea}
now: A smoke alarm is not pleasant. It is loud on purpose, so you wake up before the fire reaches you. {idea}This verse is that alarm.{/idea} {reward}It rings now so that you never hear the real sound.{/reward}
old: Verses about Hell are too heavy, so I skip them.
new: These verses are an alarm, ringing early so I can get out in time.
try: Make the short dua today: O Allah, protect me from the Fire.

title: Did no warner come to you?
subtitle: Allah does not punish without first warning
then: Ibn Kathir says these verses remind us of {idea}Allah's justice: He punishes no one until proof is established and a messenger has come{/idea}. He links it to another verse: We never punish until We have sent a messenger.
now: The same question could be asked of you: did no reminder reach you? The khutbah, the friend, the verse on your feed, this card. {reward}Each is a warner arriving, kindly, early.{/reward}
old: No one ever really explained this to me properly.
new: Allah sends warnings before anything else, and many have already reached me.
try: Think of the last reminder that reached you this week, and act on it once today.

title: Yes, a warner came, but we called him wrong.
subtitle: They heard the message and rejected it
then: They answer: {reward}yes, a warner did come to us{/reward}. But {trap}we rejected him and said Allah never sent anything, you are only in great error{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they are left with no one to blame but themselves.
now: "Religious people are just in error." It is easy to say about the cousin who started praying, or the colleague who fasts. {idea}Notice when you wave off a warner by calling them misguided.{/idea}
old: People who remind me about Allah are the ones who have it wrong.
new: When a reminder comes, I want to listen before I label the person who brought it.
try: Next time someone reminds you of something good, say jazakAllahu khayran instead of arguing.

title: If only we had listened, or used our minds.
subtitle: Two tools we already have
then: Ibn Kathir paraphrases their words: {trap}if we had benefited from our minds or listened to what Allah revealed, we would not have gone astray{/trap}. The tools were never missing. They were simply not used.
now: You have ears, and you have a mind that solves problems at work all day. {idea}Use both on the Quran: listen to one surah, and think about one verse.{/idea} {reward}That is the whole difference the verse describes.{/reward}
old: I need a big sign before I take faith seriously.
new: Listening and thinking are enough, and I already have both.
try: Listen to one verse with its translation today, then think about it for one minute.

title: They confess their sin, but too late.
subtitle: The same confession is accepted today

row.title: now
sub: Allah forgives the one who admits

then: They finally {trap}confess their sin{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}people will not be destroyed until they themselves confess their guilt{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they feel remorse when remorse no longer helps.
now: Saying "I was wrong" is one of the hardest sentences. To your parent, your spouse, your Lord. {reward}Said today, it opens a door.{/reward} {trap}Said too late, it only closes one.{/trap}
old: Admitting I was wrong makes things worse.
new: Admitting my sin now is repentance. Admitting it too late is only regret.
try: Tell Allah in your own words tonight one thing you did wrong, and ask Him to forgive it.

title: Those who fear their Lord unseen.
subtitle: The person you are when no one is watching
then: Ibn Kathir says this is someone who {idea}refrains from disobedience and does good when no one sees him except Allah{/idea}. He links it to the seven shaded on the Day: one tempted who says "I fear Allah", and one who gives charity so secretly his left hand does not know.
now: Your phone, alone, late at night. The cash register when the manager is out. The exam room when the invigilator steps away. {idea}That moment is the whole test.{/idea} {reward}Forgiveness and great reward wait on the other side.{/reward}
old: If no one will ever know, it does not really matter.
new: The moments no one sees are the ones where my fear of Allah counts most.
try: In one private moment today, choose the right thing just because Allah is there.

title: Whisper it or say it out loud, He knows.
subtitle: Even what is only in the chest
then: After the person who fears Allah in private, the surah adds: {idea}keep your words secret or say them openly{/idea}, He knows what is in the chests. Ibn Kathir says this means the ideas and thoughts that occur in hearts.
now: The voice note you sent to one friend only. The thing you muttered under your breath at your mum. The thought you would never type. {idea}All the same to Him.{/idea} {reward}So are the quiet duas no one hears.{/reward}
old: What I say in private stays private.
new: Allah hears my whispers and knows my thoughts, the bad ones and the good ones.
try: Make one silent dua today, only in your heart, knowing He hears it.

title: Would the One who created not know?
subtitle: The Maker knows what He made
then: The question comes as a simple argument: {idea}does the One who created not know?{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it as: doesn't the Creator know? He ends with two names: {reward}Al-Latif, the Subtle and Kind{/reward}, and Al-Khabir, the All-Aware.
now: You feel misunderstood: at home, at work, by friends. Even you cannot explain why you feel how you feel. {reward}The One who made you knows exactly.{/reward} {idea}And His knowing comes with gentleness.{/idea}
old: No one, not even Allah, really understands what I am going through.
new: The One who created me knows me fully and deals with me gently.
try: Tell Allah today about one feeling you have not been able to explain to anyone.

title: He made the earth easy for you. Walk and eat.
subtitle: Effort and trust walk together
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made the earth stable with springs, paths and fertile land, so {idea}travel and seek your living{/idea}. But your efforts help only if Allah makes things easy. The Prophet ﷺ said if you truly trusted Allah, {reward}He would feed you like the birds: out hungry at dawn, home full at dusk{/reward}.
now: Monday morning, the commute, the job applications, the shift. {idea}Go. Walk the paths.{/idea} {reward}But know the bread on your table is His provision, not just your payslip.{/reward} And all the roads end back with Him.
old: My income depends only on how hard I work.
new: I work hard like the bird flies out, and trust that Allah is the One who feeds me.
try: Before you leave for work or study tomorrow, say bismillah, tawakkaltu 'ala Allah at the door.

title: Do you feel safe that the ground will stay still?
subtitle: The earth that was made tame for you
then: Right after "He made the earth tame for you", the surah asks: do you feel secure it will not give way? Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}another sign of His gentleness and mercy{/reward}: He is able to punish, {reward}yet He is forbearing, pardons, and gives respite{/reward} for an appointed time.
now: You watch earthquake footage from somewhere far away, then switch to another video. {idea}The floor under your own feet is still because He holds it.{/idea} {reward}Every calm day is His patience with us.{/reward}
old: The ground under me is just solid. Nothing to think about.
new: Every steady day is Allah holding the earth still, out of patience and mercy.
try: When your feet touch the floor tomorrow morning, say alhamdulillah for the ground that holds.

title: Or safe from a storm sent from the sky?
subtitle: Then you would know what My warning meant
then: Ibn Kathir explains the storm as {trap}a wind carrying gravel{/trap}, like another verse warning of a sandstorm. Then: {idea}you shall know how My warning was{/idea}, meaning what happens to those who disregard it.
now: You check the weather app before leaving. Flood alerts, storm warnings, an amber notice. {idea}You take those seriously.{/idea} {reward}This warning comes from the One who sends the weather.{/reward}
old: I will believe it when I see it.
new: I want to learn from the warning, not from the thing it warns about.
try: Next time you see a weather warning, use it as a reminder to ask Allah for safety and forgiveness.

title: Those before them denied. How was My reproach?
subtitle: The past is evidence
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to {trap}the previous nations and old generations{/trap} who rejected. How was His rebuke and punishment of them? Great, severe and painful. {idea}The question is put to those listening now.{/idea}
now: You notice the same pattern in people around you: the shortcut that worked until it did not, the lie that held until it broke. {idea}The past is full of evidence.{/idea} {reward}Learning from it is cheaper than repeating it.{/reward}
old: What happened to others will not happen to me.
new: The record of those before me is evidence I am meant to learn from.
try: Think of one mistake you have watched someone else make. Decide today not to repeat it.

title: Look at the birds. Only the Most Merciful holds them up.
subtitle: Wings spread, wings folded, held by mercy

row.title: His mercy
sub: He made the air hold them

then: After two warnings, a gentle sign. Ibn Kathir says Allah holds the birds up {reward}by making the air serve them, out of His mercy and gentleness{/reward}. He sees what is good and suitable for every creature.
now: Pigeons on the station roof. A gull over the car park. You never look up. {idea}Each one is being held in the sky right now.{/idea} {reward}And the One holding them is the Most Merciful, watching you too.{/reward}
old: Birds flying is just normal. There is nothing to notice.
new: Every bird in the sky is held up by the Most Merciful, and so am I.
try: Watch one bird in flight today for as long as you can, and say: none holds it but Ar-Rahman.

title: Who is your army besides the Most Merciful?
subtitle: The support we think we have
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah addresses those who sought help from others besides Him: {idea}there is no protector or helper for you besides Him{/idea}. Relying on anything else is {trap}nothing but delusion{/trap}.
now: You count your safety nets: the contact who can pull strings, the savings, the family name. {trap}Useful, but they can all disappear in a week.{/trap} {reward}The Most Merciful is the only army that never retreats.{/reward}
old: My connections and savings are what really protect me.
new: Only the Most Merciful truly helps me. Everything else is a tool in His hand.
try: Before asking anyone for help today, ask Allah first.

title: Who would feed you if He held back His provision?
subtitle: Knowing it, and still turning away
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}no one gives, withholds, creates, provides and helps except Allah alone{/idea}. The Makkans knew this, he says, yet still worshipped others. {trap}They persisted in arrogance and fled from the truth.{/trap}
now: Your company announces a hiring freeze. The client pulls the contract. {idea}You suddenly see how thin the thread is.{/idea} {reward}The provision was always His. The job was just the pipe.{/reward}
old: My income comes from my job.
new: My provision comes from Allah. My job is just the way He sends it.
try: Before you eat today, pause and say: this is from Allah, not just from my wages.

title: Head down, stumbling, or upright on a straight path?
subtitle: Two ways of walking through life
then: Ibn Kathir says this is a parable of the disbeliever and the believer. The first is {trap}like someone walking bent over, not knowing where he is going{/trap}. The second {reward}stands upright, straight within himself, on a straight path{/reward}. It will look the same way on the Day of Gathering.
now: Head down at your phone, walking into people on the pavement. That is how life feels when you have no direction: reacting, bumping, scrolling. {reward}Guidance is looking up and seeing the road.{/reward}
old: As long as I keep moving, I am getting somewhere.
new: Moving with my head down is not the same as walking upright on a straight path.
try: Walk somewhere today with your phone in your pocket, looking up the whole way.

title: He gave you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little are you grateful.
subtitle: Gratitude is using the gift for Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains "hearts" as {idea}intellects and powers of reasoning{/idea}. "Little thanks you give" means {trap}how little you use these abilities to obey Him{/trap}. He created you from nothing and gave you these tools.
now: Your ears spend hours on podcasts, your eyes on screens, your mind on worries and plans. {idea}How much of that went toward Allah today?{/idea} {reward}Gratitude is turning even a little of it back to Him.{/reward}
old: Gratitude is a feeling or a word I say.
new: Real gratitude is using my hearing, sight and mind in ways that please Allah.
try: Give your ears ten minutes of Quran today, in place of something else you would have listened to.

title: He spread you over the earth, and gathers you back.
subtitle: Every language and face, one return
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}spread people through every region, with differing languages, colors, shapes and forms{/idea}. And to Him they will be gathered: brought together after this separation, just as He first made them.
now: Your workplace, your bus, your building: accents and faces from everywhere. {idea}All of them were spread here by the same Hand.{/idea} {reward}And all will stand together again before Him.{/reward}
old: People from other places are fundamentally different from me.
new: Allah spread us across the earth and will gather us all back to Him.
try: Greet someone today from a background different to yours, warmly, with a smile.

title: When is this promise, if you are truthful?
subtitle: Asking when instead of asking am I ready
then: Ibn Kathir says those who rejected the final return asked: {trap}when will this gathering after separation happen?{/trap} The demand for a date was a way to doubt it was real at all.
now: "When is the end of the world, then?" A video with a countdown, a thread arguing over signs. {idea}It feels like interest, but it can be avoidance.{/idea} {reward}The useful question is not when. It is whether you are ready.{/reward}
old: If no one can tell me when, maybe it is not real.
new: Not knowing the date is a reason to be ready every day, not a reason to doubt.
try: Ask yourself honestly tonight: if it came tomorrow, what would I want to have done today?

title: The knowledge is with Allah. I am only a clear warner.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ knew his role
then: Ibn Kathir explains the reply: {idea}no one knows the time of the Day except Allah{/idea}, but He commanded me to tell you it is real and will surely happen, so beware. {reward}I am only obligated to convey, and I have done my duty.{/reward}
now: Someone online claims to know exactly when it will be. {idea}Even the Prophet ﷺ said: that knowledge is with Allah.{/idea} {reward}What you were given is enough: it is real, so get ready.{/reward}
old: I need more details before I take the warning seriously.
new: The warning is clear enough. The date belongs to Allah, and the preparing belongs to me.
try: Ignore one end-times prediction you come across, and spend that time on one good deed instead.

title: When they see it near, their faces fall.
subtitle: This is what you kept asking for
then: Ibn Kathir says when the Day begins and they see that the matter has drawn close, {trap}it will grieve them, because they will know what awaits them{/trap}. They will be told, as a rebuke: {trap}this is what you were trying to hurry{/trap}.
now: You have joked about death, the grave, the Day, the way people joke about things that feel far away. {idea}One day it will not feel far.{/idea} {reward}Treat it with respect now, and that day your face can be bright instead.{/reward}
old: Joking about the Hereafter is harmless.
new: What feels far now will one day be close, and I want my face to be ready for it.
try: Next time you hear a joke about death or the Day, do not join in.

title: Whether we die or are shown mercy, who saves you?
subtitle: Hoping for others' downfall does not rescue you
then: Some Makkans hoped the Prophet ﷺ and his followers would be destroyed. Ibn Kathir paraphrases the reply: {idea}save yourselves, for nothing can rescue you from Allah except repentance and returning to Him{/idea}. Whatever happens to us, your own escape is your own matter.
now: You wait for the colleague you dislike to mess up. You enjoy hearing a rival family's bad news. {trap}None of it improves your own standing with Allah.{/trap} {reward}Your rescue only comes from your own turning back.{/reward}
old: If they fail, I will feel better about myself.
new: Someone else's downfall does nothing for me. Only my own return to Allah does.
try: Make a dua today for good for someone you have secretly hoped would fail.

title: He is the Most Merciful. We believe and rely on Him.
subtitle: A short creed for hard days
then: Facing mockery and threats, the Prophet ﷺ is told to answer simply. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}we believe in the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful{/idea}, and {reward}upon Him we rely in all of our affairs{/reward}. Time will show who was clearly astray.
now: A heated family argument about your faith. A coworker who keeps poking. {idea}You do not have to win every exchange.{/idea} {reward}Three calm sentences are enough: He is the Most Merciful, I believe in Him, I rely on Him.{/reward}
old: I need to win every argument about my faith.
new: I can state my belief and trust calmly and leave the outcome to Allah.
try: Memorise this line today: huwa ar-Rahmanu amanna bihi wa 'alayhi tawakkalna.

title: If your water sank away, who would bring it back?
subtitle: The surah ends with a glass of water

row.title: out of reach
sub: no axe or arm finds it

then: Ibn Kathir says if the water sank to the depths, {trap}no iron axe or strong arm could reach it{/trap}. {reward}It is only by His favor and grace that water springs up{/reward} and runs to every region in the amount people need. {idea}So all praise and thanks belong to Him.{/idea}
now: You turn on the tap without thinking. Brush your teeth, fill the kettle, rinse a cup. {reward}Every drop arrived by His favor.{/reward} {idea}The surah of the whole kingdom ends with the water in your glass.{/idea}
old: Water is just always there when I turn the tap.
new: Every drop of water I use is a gift from Allah that He could hold back.
try: Drink your next glass of water slowly, sitting down, and say alhamdulillah at the end.
